key_insight: Variantscape uses large language models to map literature-reported links between genetic variants, cancer types, and treatments at scale.
clinical_relevance: The tool may support precision oncology research and molecular tumour board preparation, but extracted associations do not establish treatment benefit.
method: Screen biomedical abstracts for gene mentions using traditional NLP.
Use LLMs to extract and standardise variant–treatment–cancer associations.
Verify associations against abstract text and assemble an open-access knowledge graph.
evidence_signal: Among 886,195 gene-containing abstracts, LLM verification identified at least one association in 35,224 papers, yielding 44,644 verified graph edges.
watch_item: Verification was LLM-based and limited to abstracts; independent expert validation and clinical utility evaluation are not reported in the supplied abstract.
paper_title: Variantscape: Retrospective Study of Large Language Model-Based Extraction of Variant-Treatment-Cancer Associations from Published Oncology Abstracts
